final_reason: Background/correction artifact. Difference images are dominated by changing diffuse background at both the physical-fit and original Stage A ephemerides. At the original 4.8-hour Stage A window, fixed-aperture depths are -6.620 +/-1.397, 5.083 +/-0.699, 7.158 +/-1.110 and -3.283 +/-1.643 ppt in sectors 58, 79, 83 and 86 [M], with raw changes tracking sky ramps and no stable isolated transit. The physical fit reaches a grazing rail and has unusably large geometry uncertainties.
assessment: KILL supported by the pixel evidence. The physical fit has b=1.099999, T14=21.307 +/-28.634 h and Rp=6.102 +/-141.165 Earth radii, with the density prior rejected at delta chi-squared 152.873 [M]. The grazing-rail problem recurs; those covariance errors are not physical confidence bounds. At that fit, aperture depths are -11.097 +/-0.666, 4.726 +/-0.331, 12.441 +/-0.442 and 4.202 +/-0.441 ppt [M]. The unchanged earlier Stage A ephemeris also shows sign changes, broad steps and ramps. Sector 58 brightens across a pre-transit step; sector 79 has broad changing structure; sector 83 steps down without isolated recovery; sector 86 follows large sky ramps. Primary differences are whole-cutout signals with no stable dimming PSF. FPP is 1.0 and NFPP 0.945597; all 18 sectors have usable centroids, with combined significance 20.367 sigma [M]. No unique eclipsing source is localized.
what_would_change: Independent photometry with a stable background must reproduce localized, repeated dimming at the candidate ephemeris and permit a constrained physical fit. Fixed-aperture depths remain diluted and their point-scatter errors omit correlated noise. The current measurements do not support a separate clean EB report.
selection: Sectors 58, 79, 83 and 86 span the first, intermediate and final epochs among sectors with complete primary and phase-0.5 windows.
scope: Final local pixel assessment, retained after the main coordinator completed C and refreshed all six Stage D catalogues. No external submission was made.

background_mask_review.scope: Supplied Gaia sources on the cutout use the same fixed mask geometry. The 300-arcsec cone covers the target aperture and the background annulus, including the two-pixel source-exclusion margin; full corner coverage of a 21-by-21-pixel square is not required for that annulus.
background_mask_review.outcome: All figures inspected. No aperture, ephemeris, detrending or science gate was tuned. Insufficient sky pixels remain explicitly unavailable.
